docs.title: The method
docs.text:
Here we explain the method of the paper (arXiv:2610.11733) and give the formulas for every quantity that minelastic computes. None of this is needed to use minelastic; the tutorials and how-to guides can be followed without it.

We first show why a few strained cells suffice, how the strain patterns are chosen and why no stress-strain scheme can use fewer. Definitions and formulas for each quantity are on separate pages: elastic constants, relaxed-ion constants, internal-strain and force-constant tensors, piezoelectric tensors, finite-temperature constants and cost.

docs.title: Stress-strain finite differences
docs.text:
A homogeneous strain \(\varepsilon\) (Voigt vector with engineering shear components) is applied to the lattice vectors of the relaxed reference cell, and the stress of the strained cell is computed. To first order, \(\sigma_i = \sum_j C_{ij}\,\varepsilon_j\). A strain pattern is a direction \(u\) in strain space, applied at \(\pm\delta\). The central difference

\[ \frac{\sigma(+\delta u) - \sigma(-\delta u)}{2\delta} = C\,u + O(\delta^2) \]

gives six linear relations between the stress components and the elastic constants. The default four-point formula, \([\sigma(-2\delta u) - 8\sigma(-\delta u) + 8\sigma(\delta u) - \sigma(2\delta u)]/12\delta\), gives the same relations with an error of order \(\delta^4\). The point group reduces \(C\) to \(n\) independent constants, from 21 (triclinic) to 3 (cubic). The question is how few patterns determine all of them.

docs.title: Symmetry-adapted form
docs.text: minelastic computes the form of \(C\) numerically from the Cartesian point-group rotations of the given cell. It group-averages the 21 symmetric unit matrices in Mandel notation, so the form holds in any orientation. Each independent constant is labelled by its leading matrix entry (c11, c12, ...), and dependent entries are written out, e.g. \(C_{66} = (c_{11}-c_{12})/2\) for hexagonal crystals (minelastic info).

docs.title: Uncoupled patterns and minimal sets
docs.text:
Let the pattern \(u\) have nonzero amplitudes on the Voigt components in its support \(S\). There are \(2^6 - 1 = 63\) possible supports. The stress component \(\sigma_i\) of the pattern is uncoupled if, for generic amplitudes on \(S\), it depends on a single independent constant. That constant then follows from one stress component of one strained cell. For a cubic crystal, the single pattern \(u = (1,0,0,1,0,0)\) (xx + yz) gives

\[ \sigma_{xx} = c_{11}\,\delta, \qquad \sigma_{yy} = \sigma_{zz} = c_{12}\,\delta, \qquad \sigma_{yz} = c_{44}\,\delta , \]

so all three constants come from one strained cell.

The paper constructs the patterns from the sparsity of the symmetry-reduced stiffness matrix, represented by an auxiliary binary matrix. A greedy procedure selects supports until every constant appears in an uncoupled stress component. Since there are only 63 supports, the minimum number can be verified by exhaustive search. minelastic accepts the greedy set for a given crystal only if it reaches the lower bound derived below, so it is provably minimal. Otherwise it searches all combinations of supports. The amplitude signs are chosen such that no uncoupled relation cancels. The resulting sets, for the standard settings:

docs.title: Extraction and consistency checks
docs.text:
• uncoupled (default): each constant is the average of all stress components that contain it alone. For cubic crystals, for example, c12 is the average from \(\sigma_{yy}\) and \(\sigma_{zz}\).
  • designated: only the first such component, as in the tables of the paper.
  • lstsq: least squares over all stress components of all patterns.

The stress components that contain several constants are not used for the extraction. They are compared with the fitted tensor and reported as checks (summary line "consistency"). A large mismatch points to nonlinearity, noise, or a reference structure that is not relaxed.

docs.title: Why fewer cells are impossible
docs.text: The strains invariant under the point group, i.e. the free lattice parameters, form a subspace \(V_0\) of dimension 6, 4, 3, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 1 for the nine types above. Every rotation maps the \(V_0\)-component of a strain onto itself. Suppose fewer strained cells were used than \(\dim V_0\). Then there is an invariant strain \(w \neq 0\) orthogonal to the \(V_0\)-components of all applied strains. Adding \(t\,w w^{\mathsf T}\) to \(C\) (in Mandel notation) leaves every computed stress unchanged, yet it is an admissible elastic tensor of the same symmetry. So \(C\) would be undetermined. The minimal uncoupled sets reach this bound in every class. No scheme, coupled or uncoupled, can use fewer strained cells.

docs.title: Internal-strain and piezoelectric tensors
docs.text:
Let a space-group operation \(\{R|t\}\) map atom \(n\) onto atom \(g(n)\). Then the forces satisfy \(F_{g(n)}(R\varepsilon R^{\mathsf T}) = R\,F_n(\varepsilon)\). The forces of the few strained cells therefore give the response of every atom to the whole symmetry orbit of the applied strains. That orbit spans all six strain components, since otherwise the elastic tensor would be undetermined by the argument above. The internal-strain tensor \(\Lambda_n = \partial F_n/\partial\varepsilon\) of every atom follows exactly, by least squares over the orbit (collect --internal-strain).

The polarization is a polar vector, \(P(R\varepsilon R^{\mathsf T}) = R\,P(\varepsilon)\), so the polarizations of the same cells determine the whole piezoelectric tensor \(e_{iJ} = \partial P_i/\partial\varepsilon_J\) in the same way. Berry-phase dipoles are defined only modulo a quantum. minelastic writes the dipole of each cell in lattice coordinates, \(p = \sum_a \varphi_a \mathbf{a}_a\), and aligns them with the reference. This gives the proper piezoelectric response, \(e = \Omega_0^{-1} A_0\, \partial\varphi/\partial\varepsilon\) (D. Vanderbilt, J. Phys. Chem. Solids 61, 147 (2000)). Clamped-ion cells give the clamped-ion tensor \(e^0\).

docs.title: Relaxed-ion response from clamped calculations
docs.text:
With atomic displacements \(u\) and strain \(\varepsilon\), the energy per cell is, to second order,

\[ E(u, \varepsilon) = \frac{\Omega}{2}\,\varepsilon^{\mathsf T} C^0 \varepsilon - u^{\mathsf T}\Lambda\,\varepsilon + \frac12\, u^{\mathsf T}\Phi\, u , \qquad P = e^0\varepsilon + \frac{1}{\Omega}\, Z^* u . \]

Here \(\Phi\) are the \(\Gamma\)-point force constants, \(\Lambda\) the internal-strain tensor, and \(Z^*\) the Born effective charges. Relaxing the ions, \(u = \Phi^{+}\Lambda\varepsilon\), gives

\[ C = C^0 - \frac{1}{\Omega}\,\Lambda^{\mathsf T}\Phi^{+}\Lambda , \qquad e = e^0 + \frac{1}{\Omega}\, Z^*\Phi^{+}\Lambda , \qquad d = e\,C^{-1} , \]

where \(\Phi^{+}\) is the inverse of \(\Phi\) on the complement of the three uniform translations (X. Wu, D. Vanderbilt and D. R. Hamann, Phys. Rev. B 72, 035105 (2005)). With --ionic, minelastic displaces only the symmetry-irreducible atoms. Each one moves along x, then y, then z, as long as the new direction enlarges the span of its images under the site symmetry. \(\Phi\) and \(Z^*\) are completed over the symmetry orbit of the displacements. \(\Lambda\) is taken from the stresses of the displaced cells (the Maxwell relation \(\partial\sigma/\partial u = -\Lambda^{\mathsf T}/\Omega\), as in VASP). The forces in the strained cells give it a second time, as a cross-check.

docs.title: Finite temperature
docs.text: At finite temperature, \(C_{ij}(T) = \partial\langle\sigma_i\rangle/\partial\varepsilon_j\), with the stresses averaged over NVT trajectories in the strained cells of the thermally expanded lattice. The strain sets are the same. See Finite temperature for the protocol, the kinetic term and the error estimates.

docs.title: Cost of the minimal sets
docs.text:
The number of strain patterns in the minimal set equals the number of lattice parameters that the symmetry leaves free, and no stress-strain scheme can use fewer (proof sketch). The usual approach, used by VASP's IBRION = 6 and by most workflows, applies the six single-component strains. Both apply every pattern at the same step sizes: four by default in minelastic (\(\pm\delta\), \(\pm 2\delta\), as VASP's NFREE = 4) and two with --stencil central (as NFREE = 2). The saving is therefore the ratio of the pattern counts.

Most materials of interest are in the last four rows. The paper also compares the minimal sets with earlier tabulated schemes, which need more configurations for several symmetry types.

docs.text:
Everything that minelastic computes is built on the same strained cells, so every quantity inherits the factor above. \(n\) is the number of patterns, \(p\) the number of steps per pattern (4 or 2) and \(D\) the number of symmetry-irreducible atomic displacements.

For wurtzite AlN (\(n = 2\), \(D = 4\)) and two points per strain, --ionic needs 4 + 8 = 12 single points where VASP's IBRION = 6 needs 12 + 8 = 20. For fcc Al at finite temperature it is 2 MD runs instead of 12, the largest saving in absolute terms, since every cell is a full molecular-dynamics run.

docs.text:
Wall times of the clamped-ion runs of wurtzite AlN in the tutorials (VASP, Quantum ESPRESSO, ABINIT), with the same settings for both sets (two points per strain, one 32-core node):

docs.title: Elastic constants
docs.text:
Stress and strain are 6-vectors in Voigt order xx, yy, zz, yz, xz, xy, with engineering shear strains:

\[ \sigma = (\sigma_{xx}, \sigma_{yy}, \sigma_{zz}, \sigma_{yz}, \sigma_{xz}, \sigma_{xy}), \qquad \varepsilon = (\varepsilon_{xx}, \varepsilon_{yy}, \varepsilon_{zz}, 2\varepsilon_{yz}, 2\varepsilon_{xz}, 2\varepsilon_{xy}). \]

\(\sigma\) is the Cauchy stress in GPa, positive in tension. The elastic constants are its derivatives at the stress-free reference structure,

\[ C_{ij} = \left.\frac{\partial \sigma_i}{\partial \varepsilon_j}\right|_{\varepsilon = 0}, \qquad i, j = 1, \dots, 6 . \]

With the fractional coordinates of the atoms held fixed they are the clamped-ion constants \(C^0\); Relaxed ions adds the relaxation of the atoms.

Strained cells. A strain pattern is a 6-vector \(u_k\). Pattern \(k\) at the amplitude \(m\delta\) deforms the lattice vectors \(a_i\) of the reference cell as

\[ a_i' = F a_i, \qquad F = I + \varepsilon(m\delta u_k), \]

where \(\varepsilon(\cdot)\) is the symmetric strain tensor of a Voigt vector (no rigid rotation). The fractional coordinates of the atoms are kept.

Finite differences. The response of pattern \(k\) is

\[ r_k = \frac{1}{\delta} \sum_m g_m\, \sigma(m\delta u_k) = C u_k + O(\delta^4), \]

with \(m = (-2, -1, 1, 2)\) and \(g = (1, -8, 8, -1)/12\) for the default four-point formula, or \(m = (-1, 1)\), \(g = (-1/2, 1/2)\) and an error of order \(\delta^2\) for the two-point (central) formula. The default step is \(\delta = 0.01\).

Symmetry. The point group of the crystal (with magnetic order, if any) restricts \(C\) to

\[ C = \sum_{p=1}^{n} c_p B_p , \]

with \(n\) independent constants, from 21 for triclinic to 3 for cubic crystals. Each constant \(c_p\) is named after the leading entry of its basis matrix \(B_p\) (c11, c12, ...), and the basis is computed from the point-group rotations of the given cell (Method). Each response gives six linear relations

\[ r_{ki} = \sum_p a_{kip}\, c_p, \qquad a_{kip} = (B_p u_k)_i . \]

Extraction. In a minimal uncoupled set every constant appears alone in at least one relation, so \(c_p = r_{ki}/a_{kip}\). The default method uncoupled averages \(c_p\) over all such relations, designated takes the first one, and lstsq fits all relations by weighted least squares. The relations that contain more than one constant are not needed; minelastic reports the largest residual \(|r_{ki} - \sum_p a_{kip} c_p|\) as a consistency check. For hexagonal crystals the two patterns \(u_1\) = xx + yz and \(u_2\) = zz give

\[ r_1 = (c_{11},\ c_{12},\ c_{13},\ c_{44},\ 0,\ 0), \qquad r_2 = (c_{13},\ c_{13},\ c_{33},\ 0,\ 0,\ 0), \]

so c13 is obtained twice.

Moduli and stability. With \(S = C^{-1}\), the Voigt and Reuss bounds of the bulk and shear moduli are

\[ K_V = \frac{C_{11} + C_{22} + C_{33} + 2(C_{12} + C_{23} + C_{13})}{9}, \qquad G_V = \frac{C_{11} + C_{22} + C_{33} - (C_{12} + C_{23} + C_{13}) + 3(C_{44} + C_{55} + C_{66})}{15}, \] \[ \frac{1}{K_R} = S_{11} + S_{22} + S_{33} + 2(S_{12} + S_{23} + S_{13}), \qquad \frac{15}{G_R} = 4(S_{11} + S_{22} + S_{33}) - 4(S_{12} + S_{23} + S_{13}) + 3(S_{44} + S_{55} + S_{66}), \]

with the Hill averages \(K = (K_V + K_R)/2\) and \(G = (G_V + G_R)/2\), Young's modulus \(E = 9KG/(3K + G)\), Poisson's ratio \(\nu = (3K - 2G)/(2(3K + G))\) and the universal anisotropy index \(A_U = 5 G_V/G_R + K_V/K_R - 6\). The crystal is Born stable if all eigenvalues of \(C\) are positive.

Stress measure. VASP's IBRION = 6 differentiates \(J\sigma\) with \(J = \det F\); stress_measure="kirchhoff" (--stress-measure kirchhoff) does the same. For a stress-free reference both give the same constants.

docs.title: Finite temperature
docs.text:
At temperature \(T\) the elastic constants are the strain derivatives of the thermally averaged stress,

\[ C_{ij}(T) = \left.\frac{\partial \langle \sigma_i \rangle_T}{\partial \varepsilon_j}\right|_{\varepsilon = 0}, \]

taken at the thermally expanded reference cell, with the cell held fixed in every strained state. These are isothermal constants. The minimal strain sets apply unchanged; only the stress of each strained cell becomes an average. The protocol of the paper is:

  1. Lattice at \(T\). An NPT run at zero pressure gives the thermally expanded cell. Most of the softening of the elastic constants with temperature comes from thermal expansion, so the expanded cell, not the 0 K one, is strained.
  2. Strained cells at \(T\). NVT runs with the cell held fixed (NPT would undo the strain), one in each strained cell of the minimal set.

  3. Constants. For the states \(x\) of pattern \(k\) (amplitudes \(m_x\delta\)), with \(n_x\) samples of the stress (MD steps after equilibration, block averages, or snapshots), the mean stresses \(\bar\sigma_x\) give

    \[ r_k = \frac{1}{\delta} \sum_x g_x\, \bar\sigma_x, \qquad \mathrm{Cov}(r_k) = \frac{1}{\delta^2} \sum_x g_x^2\, \frac{S_x}{n_x}, \]

    with the finite-difference weights \(g_x\) and the sample covariance matrix \(S_x\) of the six stress components. The constants follow from the \(r_k\) as at 0 K (Elastic constants), and their standard errors from \(\mathrm{Cov}(r_k)\), correlations between the components of one pattern included. The formula assumes uncorrelated samples, so block-average or thin long trajectories.

MD inputs use the two-point formula (\(\pm\delta\)) by default. The four-point weights \((1, -8, 8, -1)/12\) amplify the noise of the averages: at equal total MD time the result is about twice as noisy.

Kinetic stress. The Cauchy stress of an MD run contains the kinetic term \(-n k_B T\, \delta_{ij}\) with \(n = N/V\). Under a normal strain \(V\) changes by the factor \(1 + \varepsilon_j\), so this term adds

\[ \frac{\partial (-n k_B T)}{\partial \varepsilon_j} = n k_B T \qquad (i, j \le 3) \]

to \(C_{ij}\) (about 0.25 GPa for Al at 300 K). VASP and pw.x print the stress of the instantaneous configuration without it; --kinetic-temperature T (kinetic_temperature=T) adds the term. With stress_measure="kirchhoff" the kinetic part of \(J\sigma\) is \(-N k_B T/V_0\), independent of the strain, and nothing is added.

Isothermal and adiabatic. Fixed-cell NVT runs give isothermal constants; ultrasonic experiments measure adiabatic ones, \(C^S_{ij} = C^T_{ij} + T V \lambda_i \lambda_j / C_V\) with the thermal stress coefficients \(\lambda_i = \partial \sigma_i / \partial T|_\varepsilon\) and the heat capacity \(C_V\) of the cell. For cubic crystals \(\lambda_1 = \lambda_2 = \lambda_3\), so only c11 and c12 differ (through the bulk modulus), not c44 or (c11 - c12)/2.

docs.title: Internal strain and force constants
docs.text:
The internal-strain tensor is the force on each atom per unit strain at fixed fractional coordinates,

\[ \Lambda_{n\alpha, J} = \left.\frac{\partial F_{n\alpha}}{\partial \varepsilon_J}\right|_{\varepsilon = 0}, \]

for atom \(n\), Cartesian direction \(\alpha\) and Voigt strain component \(J\) (engineering shear), in eV/Å per unit strain. The net force vanishes, so \(\sum_n \Lambda_n = 0\). minelastic obtains it in two ways.

  1. From the strained cells, without further calculations. The force responses of each pattern, \(f_k = \delta^{-1} \sum_m g_m F(m\delta u_k)\), use the same finite-difference formula as the stresses. If a space-group operation \(\{R|t\}\) maps atom \(n\) onto atom \(g(n)\), the forces obey

    \[ F_{g(n)}(R \varepsilon R^T) = R\, F_n(\varepsilon) . \]

    The computed patterns therefore give the response of every atom to the whole orbit of strains \(\{R^T \varepsilon_k R\}\). This orbit spans all six strain components whenever the patterns determine \(C\), so the minimal set gives the complete tensor; \(\Lambda_n\) follows by least squares over the orbit.

  2. From displaced atoms (ionic=True). The mixed second derivative of the energy taken in the other order gives

    \[ \Lambda_{n\beta, J} = -\Omega\, \frac{\partial \sigma_J}{\partial u_{n\beta}} , \]

    from the stresses of the cells in which atom \(n\) is displaced along \(\beta\) (the route of VASP's IBRION = 6).

The displaced atoms also give the \(\Gamma\)-point force constants

\[ \Phi_{m\alpha, n\beta} = -\frac{\partial F_{m\alpha}}{\partial u_{n\beta}} \]

in eV/Å\(^2\). Only the symmetry-irreducible displacements are computed: for the first atom of each orbit, the Cartesian directions x, y, z are kept as long as they add a new direction to the images under its site group, as VASP chooses them. The other atoms and directions follow from \(F_{g(m)} = R F_m\), and \(\Phi\) is symmetrized as a \(3N \times 3N\) matrix. The relaxation of the atoms per unit strain is

\[ u = \Phi^+ \Lambda \]

in Å, with \(\Phi^+\) the inverse of \(\Phi\) on the complement of the uniform translations. It enters the relaxed-ion constants (Relaxed ions) and the piezoelectric tensor (Born charges and piezoelectricity).

docs.title: Piezoelectricity
docs.text:
The piezoelectric stress tensor is the change of the polarization \(P = d/\Omega\) (dipole moment \(d\) of the cell per volume) with strain,

\[ e_{iJ} = \frac{\partial P_i}{\partial \varepsilon_J} \]

in C/m\(^2\), for Cartesian direction \(i\) and Voigt strain component \(J\). The strain coefficients follow with the relaxed-ion compliance \(S = C^{-1}\),

\[ d = e\, S \]

in pC/N, and the Born effective charges are the dipole change per atomic displacement,

\[ Z^*_{n, \alpha\beta} = \frac{\partial d_\alpha}{\partial u_{n\beta}} \]

in units of the elementary charge. Charge neutrality requires \(\sum_n Z^*_n = 0\) (acoustic sum rule); minelastic reports the sum as a convergence check.

Proper response. A Berry-phase polarization is defined modulo a quantum. minelastic writes the dipole of each cell in lattice coordinates, \(d = \sum_a \phi_a a_a\), brings the \(\phi_a\) of all cells of a pattern to one branch (\(\phi \to \phi - q\, \mathrm{round}((\phi - \phi_{\mathrm{prev}})/q)\), in order of increasing strain), and differentiates

\[ e_{iJ} = \frac{1}{\Omega_0} \sum_a a^0_{a,i}\, \frac{\partial \phi_a}{\partial \varepsilon_J}, \]

with the lattice vectors \(a^0_a\) and the volume \(\Omega_0\) of the reference cell (Vanderbilt, J. Phys. Chem. Solids 61, 147 (2000)). Unlike the derivative of \(P\) itself (the improper tensor), this proper tensor does not depend on the branch of the polarization.

Clamped ions. The dipoles of the strained cells give the clamped-ion tensor \(e^0\) with the same finite-difference formula as the stresses. The polarization is a polar vector, \(P(R\varepsilon R^T) = R\, P(\varepsilon)\) for every point-group rotation \(R\), so the responses of the computed patterns determine the whole tensor by least squares over their symmetry orbits, as for the internal-strain tensor.

Relaxed ions. The displaced atoms give \(Z^*\) from their dipoles. With the relaxation per unit strain \(u = \Phi^+ \Lambda\) (Relaxed ions), the polarization \(P = e^0 \varepsilon + Z^* u/\Omega\) gives the total (relaxed-ion) tensor

\[ e = e^0 + \frac{1}{\Omega}\, Z^* \Phi^+ \Lambda . \]

With \(Z^*\) in units of \(e\), \(\Phi^+\Lambda\) in Å and \(\Omega\) in Å\(^3\), the second term is in \(e\)/Å\(^2\) (1 \(e\)/Å\(^2\) = 16.02 C/m\(^2\)).

The dipoles can come from a Berry-phase calculation (read from VASP with LCALCPOL), from any function of the atoms (calculate(..., dipole=f)), or be passed to ElasticSetup.compute(..., polarization=...). Instead, \(Z^*\) and \(e^0\) can be taken from a DFPT run of the reference structure.

docs.title: Relaxed ions
docs.text:
A strain moves the atoms that are not fixed by symmetry. To second order in the atomic displacements \(u\) (3N components) and the strain \(\varepsilon\), the energy of a cell of volume \(\Omega\) is

\[ E(u, \varepsilon) = E_0 + \frac{\Omega}{2}\, \varepsilon \cdot C^0 \varepsilon - u \cdot \Lambda \varepsilon + \frac{1}{2}\, u \cdot \Phi u , \]

with the clamped-ion constants \(C^0\), the internal-strain tensor \(\Lambda = \partial F/\partial \varepsilon\) and the \(\Gamma\)-point force constants \(\Phi = -\partial F/\partial u\) (Internal strain). The forces \(F = -\partial E/\partial u = \Lambda\varepsilon - \Phi u\) vanish for

\[ u = \Phi^+ \Lambda\, \varepsilon , \]

where \(\Phi^+\) is the inverse of \(\Phi\) on the complement of the three uniform translations. The stress \(\sigma = \Omega^{-1}\, \partial E/\partial \varepsilon\) at these positions gives the relaxed-ion constants

\[ C = C^0 - \frac{1}{\Omega}\, \Lambda^T \Phi^+ \Lambda . \]

With \(\Lambda\) in eV/Å, \(\Phi\) in eV/Å\(^2\) and \(\Omega\) in Å\(^3\), the second term is in eV/Å\(^3\) (1 eV/Å\(^3\) = 160.2 GPa). minelastic computes \(C\) in one of two ways.

  1. Relaxing the ions (relax_ions=True, --relax-ions). The atoms of every strained cell are relaxed at fixed cell, and the stresses are differentiated as for \(C^0\). The relaxation at finite strain also contains terms beyond linear order; the four-point formula removes them to order \(\delta^4\).
  2. Clamped single points (ionic=True, --ionic), the route of VASP's IBRION = 6. The strained cells give \(C^0\). The symmetry-irreducible atoms, displaced by \(\pm h\) and \(\pm 2h\) (default \(h\) = 0.01 Å), give \(\Phi\) from their forces and \(\Lambda\) from their stresses. \(C\) follows from the formula above, as the exact linear response. If \(\Phi\) has an unstable or soft optical mode, the relaxed-ion response is undefined and minelastic stops with an error.

The second route needs no relaxations. Relaxations are costly, and they must be converged tightly: the forces that a strain of 0.01 induces are only about 0.05 eV/Å.
